newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht strong offshore, interbank steady late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht strong offshore, interbank steady late.

text.p: The Thai baht remained strong against the dollar in late Thursday trade on strong offshore demand for baht by players attempting to cover their short positions, dealers said.

The baht was traded at 24.00/24.10 to the dollar in the offshore market compared with 23.900/24.00 in the early morning. The baht/dollar spot rate offshore early on Thursday was the highest since Thailand's last baht devaluation in 1984.
In the local market, the baht was traded lower at 25.820/25.840 in late trade versus 25.835/25.840 in the early morning.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate unchanged at 25.82 per dollar.
"Demand for baht remained strong among offshore players. But the trade was very quiet in the local market," said one dealer at a foreign bank.

A two-tier offshore and onshore baht market has been in place since mid-May after speculative attacks on the currency prompted the BOT to impose what dealers called capital controls to cut off baht supply to offshore speculators.
As offshore players scrambled for baht, the central bank denied market talk that it would buy dollars in offshore markets at 24.00 baht to help bail out speculators caught short of baht.
Dealers said the denial was aimed at hitting back at speculators who led the baht attack and held positions against the currency.
The baht/dollar one-month swap premium was traded at 150/170 satangs per dollar in offshore and 18/25 in domestic market.
The overnight interbank rate was steady at 15.00-15.50 late, unchanged from early morning trade, dealers said.
Dealers said interbank rates would stay high for the rest of this week due to strong demand for funds for mid-year corporate tax payments and to meet central bank reserve requirements due this week.
